meta.authored: Read from the held Act, section by section. NOT generated from master sheet.xlsx - ca_master.json is, and must not be hand-edited (SS2k). This file carries obligations the generated corpus does not, found by the completeness measurement in SS3x: 49 of 497 sections were cited by any rule. Every rule quotes the words it came from.
meta.method: The Act's own chapters did the first cut. Chapters II to XIII run from incorporation to managerial remuneration and are where a company's recurring and registrable duties live; Chapter XIV onward is inspection, compromises, oppression, winding up, Tribunal and offences - event-driven, or about someone other than the company. Within those chapters: 193 sections impose a duty, 51 were already cited, 142 were not, and 96 of those state a period or name a return. Those 96 were read and eleven are obligations on the COMPANY with a period the Act itself states.
meta.excluded: s.84 states thirty days but the duty is on the person who obtains the receiver's appointment, not on the company - the company is the recipient of the notice. s.13's fifteen days was substituted away by Act 1 of 2018 and the held text does not make the current period plain. s.58, s.59, s.62, s.66, s.68 and s.74 run through the Tribunal or through multi-stage offers rather than a filing deadline. Punishment and liability sections (s.34-38, s.86, s.127, s.147) are consequences, not obligations.
meta.stale: The Act held here is amended only to 01.04.2021 - over five years old. Any period below must be re-checked against a current compilation before it is relied on. This is SS2c's standing warning and it applies to every rule in this file.

rules.title: Declaration of commencement of business within 180 days of incorporation
rules.detail: A company with share capital may not commence business or exercise borrowing powers until a director files a declaration that every subscriber has paid the value of the shares agreed to be taken, and the company has filed verification of its registered office under s.12(2).
rules.quote: A company incorporated after the commencement of the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2019 and having a share capital shall not commence any business or exercise any borrowing powers unless - (a) a declaration is filed by a director within a period of one hundred and eighty days of the date of incorporation of the company ... with the Registrar that every subscriber to the memorandum has paid the value of the shares agreed to be taken by him
rules.timelineText: Within one hundred and eighty days of the date of incorporation
rules.appliesToText: Company having a share capital, incorporated after the Companies (Amendment) Act 2019
rules.evidence: Filed declaration with SRN; bank statement evidencing subscription money; registered office verification
rules.notes: Two limbs, and the second is easy to lose: the declaration under (a) AND the registered office verification under s.12(2) referred to in (b). Until both are done the company may not commence business or borrow. The form is prescribed by Rules not held here. This is a ONE-TIME obligation dated from incorporation, and this app does not hold an incorporation date as a field - the year is in the CIN but not the day - so no date is computed.

rules.title: File altered articles with the Registrar within fifteen days
rules.detail: Every alteration of the articles, with the Central Government's approval order where required, must be filed with the Registrar together with a printed copy of the altered articles.
rules.quote: Every alteration of the articles under this section and a copy of the order of the Central Government approving the alteration as per sub-section (1) shall be filed with the Registrar, together with a printed copy of the altered articles, within a period of fifteen days in such manner as may be prescribed
rules.timelineText: Within a period of fifteen days

due.when: Within fifteen days of the alteration

rules.appliesToText: Every company altering its articles
rules.evidence: Filed form with SRN; printed copy of altered articles; special resolution
rules.notes: Runs alongside the s.117(3)(a) filing of the special resolution itself, which the register already carries. Two filings, one event.

rules.title: Send copies of the memorandum and articles to a member within seven days of request
rules.detail: On a member's request and on payment of the prescribed fee, send a copy of the memorandum, the articles and every agreement and resolution referred to in s.117(1) where those have been filed.
rules.quote: A company shall, on being so requested by a member, send to him within seven days of the request and subject to the payment of such fees as may be prescribed, a copy of each of the following documents
rules.timelineText: Within seven days of the request

due.when: Within seven days of the member's request

rules.appliesToText: Every company, on a member's request
rules.evidence: Request register with date received and date despatched
rules.notes: Seven days from the REQUEST, not from payment of the fee. This app holds no register of member requests, so no date is computed - record it against the request.

rules.title: Notice to the Registrar of alteration of share capital within thirty days
rules.detail: File notice in the prescribed form where the company alters its share capital, where a Government order has the effect of increasing authorised capital, or where the company redeems redeemable preference shares - with an altered memorandum.
rules.quote: the company shall file a notice in the prescribed form with the Registrar within a period of thirty days of such alteration or increase or redemption, as the case may be, along with an altered memorandum
rules.timelineText: Within a period of thirty days of the alteration, increase or redemption

due.when: Within thirty days of the alteration

rules.appliesToText: Every company altering, increasing or redeeming share capital
rules.evidence: Filed notice with SRN; altered memorandum; board and member resolutions
rules.notes: Three separate triggers in one sub-section, and REDEMPTION of preference shares is the one usually forgotten because it feels like a repayment rather than an alteration of capital.

rules.title: Call an extraordinary general meeting on a valid members' requisition
rules.detail: On a valid requisition by members holding the prescribed tenth, the Board must proceed within twenty-one days to call a meeting to be held not later than forty-five days from receipt of the requisition. If it does not, the requisitionists may call the meeting themselves within three months.
rules.quote: If the Board does not, within twenty-one days from the date of receipt of a valid requisition in regard to any matter, proceed to call a meeting for the consideration of that matter on a day not later than forty-five days from the date of receipt of such requisition, the meeting may be called and held by the requisitionists themselves within a period of three months from the date of the requisition
rules.timelineText: Board to proceed within twenty-one days; meeting not later than forty-five days from receipt of the requisition

due.when: Board proceeds within 21 days; meeting within 45 days of the requisition

rules.appliesToText: Every company receiving a valid members' requisition
rules.evidence: Requisition with date of receipt; board resolution calling the meeting; notice
rules.notes: TWO clocks from one event: twenty-one days for the Board to act, and forty-five days for the meeting itself. Missing the first hands the members the right to call the meeting - and to be reimbursed - so this is not a filing deadline but a loss of control.

rules.title: Furnish minutes of a general meeting to a member within seven working days
rules.detail: A member is entitled to a copy of the minutes of any general meeting within seven working days of requesting it, on payment of the prescribed fee.
rules.quote: Any member shall be entitled to be furnished, within seven working days after he has made a request in that behalf to the company, and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed, with a copy of any minutes referred to in sub-section (1)
rules.timelineText: Within seven working days after the request

due.when: Within seven working days of the member's request

rules.appliesToText: Every company, on a member's request
rules.notes: WORKING days, not calendar days - and this app holds no holiday calendar, so even if the request were recorded the date could not be computed exactly. Same limitation the register states for Reg 52(8) under LODR.

rules.title: Report on the annual general meeting - MGT-15 - within thirty days of the AGM
rules.detail: A listed public company must prepare a report on each annual general meeting confirming that the meeting was convened, held and conducted as per the Act and the rules, and file a copy with the Registrar within thirty days of the conclusion of the meeting.
rules.quote: Every listed public company shall prepare in the prescribed manner a report on each annual general meeting including the confirmation to the effect that the meeting was convened, held and conducted as per the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder. (2) The company shall file with the Registrar a copy of the report referred to in sub-section (1) within thirty days of the conclusion of the annual general meeting
rules.timelineText: Within thirty days of the conclusion of the annual general meeting
rules.appliesToText: Every listed public company
rules.evidence: Signed report; filed form with SRN
rules.notes: LISTED PUBLIC COMPANIES ONLY - the section says so in terms. Falls on the same thirty days as AOC-4 under s.137 and is routinely missed because AOC-4 draws the attention. The form is prescribed by Rules not held here.

rules.title: Transfer unpaid or unclaimed dividend to the Unpaid Dividend Account
rules.detail: Where a declared dividend has not been paid or claimed within thirty days of declaration, transfer the total unpaid or unclaimed amount to a special account called the Unpaid Dividend Account, within seven days of that thirty-day period expiring.
rules.quote: Where a dividend has been declared by a company but has not been paid or claimed within thirty days from the date of the declaration to any shareholder entitled to the payment of the dividend, the company shall, within seven days from the date of expiry of the said period of thirty days, transfer the total amount of dividend which remains unpaid or unclaimed to a special account to be opened by the company in that behalf in any scheduled bank to be called the Unpaid Dividend Account
rules.timelineText: Within seven days of the expiry of thirty days from declaration - i.e. by day 37

due.when: Seven days after the thirty days from declaration expire

rules.appliesToText: Every company that has declared a dividend
rules.evidence: Bank statement for the Unpaid Dividend Account; transfer advice; dividend register
rules.notes: A COMPOUND period, and the shape is what catches people: thirty days from declaration, THEN seven days to transfer - thirty-seven days in all, not thirty and not seven. The section continues into the statement of unpaid amounts on the website and the eventual transfer to the IEPF after seven years; those limbs are not separately carried here.

rules.title: Periodical financial results - file with the Registrar within thirty days
rules.detail: Where the Central Government requires a prescribed class of unlisted companies to prepare periodical financial results, those results must be approved by the Board, audited or limited-reviewed, and a copy filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the end of the relevant period.
rules.quote: file a copy with the Registrar within a period of thirty days of completion of the relevant period with such fees as may be prescribed
rules.timelineText: Within a period of thirty days of completion of the relevant period

due.when: Within thirty days of the end of the relevant period

rules.appliesToText: Such class of unlisted companies as the Central Government may require
rules.evidence: Board approval; audit or limited review report; filed copy with SRN
rules.notes: APPLICABILITY IS NOT SETTLED HERE. s.129A opens 'The Central Government may, require such class or classes of unlisted companies as may be prescribed' - so whether it bites at all depends on a notification not held in reference/. Carried so the question is visible rather than absent, and flagged for review. The period itself is stated in the section.

rules.title: Furnish directors' DINs to the Registrar within fifteen days
rules.detail: Within fifteen days of receiving a director's intimation of DIN under s.156, furnish the Director Identification Numbers of all its directors to the Registrar.
rules.quote: Every company shall, within fifteen days of the receipt of intimation under section 156, furnish the Director Identification Number of all its directors to the Registrar or any other officer or authority as may be specified by the Central Government with such fees as may be prescribed
rules.frequency: On receipt of a DIN intimation
rules.timelineText: Within fifteen days of the receipt of intimation under section 156

due.when: Within fifteen days of the director's DIN intimation

rules.appliesToText: Every company
rules.evidence: Director's s.156 intimation with date received; filed form with SRN
rules.notes: The clock runs from the COMPANY's receipt of the director's intimation, not from the DIN being allotted. s.157(2) makes the company liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees, with a further one hundred rupees for each day after the first - the same shape as s.92(5) and s.137(3).

rules.title: Inform the Registrar of contracts with the sole member within fifteen days
rules.detail: A One Person Company must inform the Registrar of every contract entered into with its sole member who is also a director, as recorded in the minutes of the Board meeting, within fifteen days of the Board's approval.
rules.quote: The company shall inform the Registrar about every contract entered into by the company and recorded in the minutes of the meeting of its Board of Directors under sub-section (1) within a period of fifteen days of the date of approval by the Board of Directors
rules.frequency: Per contract with the sole member
rules.timelineText: Within a period of fifteen days of the date of approval by the Board

due.when: Within fifteen days of Board approval

rules.appliesToText: One Person Company contracting with its sole member who is also a director
rules.evidence: Board minutes recording the contract; intimation to the Registrar with SRN
rules.notes: ONE PERSON COMPANIES ONLY, and only for contracts with the sole member who is also a director. s.193(1) excludes contracts entered into in the ordinary course of business, so not every contract triggers this. The fifteen days runs from BOARD APPROVAL, not from the contract date.

rules.title: Call a general meeting on not less than clear twenty-one days' notice, in writing or by electronic mode
rules.detail: "Clear" days exclude both the day the notice is served and the day of the meeting, so twenty-one clear days is longer than twenty-one days. The proviso allows a shorter notice with the consent of the prescribed majority of members, which is a fact about the meeting and not a period -- so it is named rather than modelled. The app already computes with this period: SS3d anchors the annual report to the AGM less twenty-one clear days, because Reg 36(1) sends the report with the notice. The register itself had never stated it.
rules.quote: A general meeting of a company may be called by giving not less than clear twenty -one days
rules.timelineText: Not less than clear twenty-one days before the meeting
rules.appliesToText: Every company calling a general meeting
rules.evidence: The notice, and proof of the date it was issued
rules.notes: Counted backwards from a meeting the company fixes, so no date is computed -- the register holds no planned meeting date. The period runs BACKWARD from the meeting, so treating clear days as calendar days would produce a LATER last date than the Act allows (SS3z).

rules.title: Reimburse the requisitionists the reasonable expenses of a meeting the Board failed to call, and recover the sum from the defaulting directors fee
rules.detail: Arises only where the Board did not act on a valid requisition under s.100(4). The Act requires the company to reimburse AND to deduct the sum from the fee or other remuneration payable to the directors who defaulted.
rules.quote: Any reasonable expenses incurred by the requisitionists in call ing a meeting under sub -section ( 4) shall be reimbursed to the requisitionists by the company and the sums so paid shall be deducted from any fee or other remuneration under section 197 payable to such of the directors who were in default in calling the me eting. 101. Notice of meeting.
rules.appliesToText: Every company other than a One Person Company, which holds no general meeting, where a requisitioned meeting was called by the requisitionists themselves

rules.title: Within ninety days of transferring an amount to the Unpaid Dividend Account, prepare a statement of the names, last known addresses and unpaid dividend of each person, and place it on the company website
rules.detail: The ninety days runs from the transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account, which itself is due within seven days after the thirty days in s.124(1). This app does not record the dividend declaration, so the date cannot be computed - the period is certain and the anchor is not held.
rules.quote: The company shall, within a period of ninety days of making any transfer of an amount under sub - section ( 1) to the Unpaid Dividend Account, prepare a statement containing the names, their last known addresses and the unpaid dividend to be paid to each person and place it on the website of the company, if any, and also on any other website approved by the Central Government for this purpose, in such form, manner and other particulars as may be prescribed.
rules.frequency: On a transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account
rules.timelineText: Within ninety days of the transfer

due.when: An amount is transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account

rules.appliesToText: Every company that has transferred an amount to the Unpaid Dividend Account

rules.title: Pay interest at twelve per cent per annum on any amount not transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account, from the date of default, for the benefit of the members in proportion to the amount remaining unpaid
rules.detail: The interest runs to the MEMBERS, not to the Government. It accrues from the date of default, so it is a growing liability rather than a fixed penalty.
rules.quote: If an y default is made in transferring the total amount referred to in sub -section ( 1) or any part thereof to the Unpaid Dividend Account of the company, it shall pay, from the date of such default, interest on so much of the amount as has not been transferred to the said account, at the rate of twelve per cent.
rules.appliesToText: Every company that has defaulted in transferring to the Unpaid Dividend Account

rules.title: Transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund any money in the Unpaid Dividend Account that remains unpaid or unclaimed for seven years from the date of transfer, together with interest accrued, and send a statement of the details
rules.detail: Seven years from the transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account, not from the declaration. A retention-then-transfer duty with a very long clock, which is exactly why it is missed - the person who declared the dividend has usually left by the time it falls.
rules.quote: Any money transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account of a company in pursuance of this secti on which remains unpaid or unclaimed for a period of seven years from the date of such transfer shall be transferred by the company along with interest accrued, if any, thereon to the Fund established under sub-section ( 1) of section 125 and the co mpany shall send a statement in the prescribed form of the details of such transfer to the authority which administers the said Fund and that authority shall issue a receipt to
rules.frequency: On the seventh anniversary of each transfer
rules.timelineText: Seven years from the date of transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account

due.when: Money has been in the Unpaid Dividend Account for seven years

rules.appliesToText: Every company holding money in an Unpaid Dividend Account

rules.title: Transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund all SHARES on which dividend has not been paid or claimed for seven consecutive years, with a statement of the details
rules.detail: The SHARES themselves, not only the dividend. Seven CONSECUTIVE years of unpaid or unclaimed dividend, so a single year of payment resets the count. The shareholder may claim the shares back from the Fund.
rules.quote: All shares in respect of which1[dividend has not been paid or claimed for seven consecutive years or more shall be] transferred by the company in the name of Investor Education and Protection Fund along with a statement containing such details as may be prescribed: Provided that any claim ant of shares transferred above shall be entitled to claim the transfer of shares from Investor Education and Protection Fund in accordance with such procedure and on submission of such documents as may be prescribed.
rules.frequency: On seven consecutive years of unclaimed dividend

due.when: Dividend on a share is unpaid or unclaimed for seven consecutive years

rules.appliesToText: Every company with shares carrying dividend unpaid or unclaimed for seven consecutive years

rules.title: The Board of Directors shall lay the financial statements for the financial year before every annual general meeting
rules.detail: The duty to LAY them, as distinct from preparing them under s.129(1) or filing them under s.137. An OPC has no AGM, so this does not reach one.
rules.quote: At every a nnual general meeting of a company, the Board of Directors of the company shall lay before such meeting financial statements for the financial year.
rules.appliesToText: Every company other than a One Person Company, which holds no annual general meeting

rules.title: Where the financial statements do not comply with the accounting standards, disclose in them the deviation, the reasons for it, and its financial effects
rules.detail: Not a permission to deviate - a requirement to disclose the deviation, the reasons AND the financial effects if it happens. All three.
rules.quote: Without prejudice to sub -section ( 1), where the financial statements of a company do not comply with the accounting standards referred to in sub -section ( 1), the company shall disclose in its financial statements, the deviation f rom the accounting standards, the reasons for such deviation and the financial effects, if any, arising out of such deviation.
rules.appliesToText: Every company whose financial statements deviate from the accounting standards

rules.title: At least one director must have stayed in India for not less than 182 days during the financial year
rules.detail: The RESIDENT DIRECTOR test. calcBoardCheck reports it as "not tested" because the directors register holds no residency field - so the obligation existed in the calculator as an untested row and on no register row at all. A newly incorporated company applies the proviso: the period is counted proportionately from incorporation.
rules.quote: Every company shall have at least one director who stays in India for a total period of not less than one hundred and eighty -two days during the financial year:
rules.appliesToText: Every company

rules.title: The company AND its independent directors must abide by the Code for Independent Directors in Schedule IV
rules.detail: Schedule IV is the Code: the guidelines of professional conduct, the role and functions, the duties, the manner of appointment, re-appointment, resignation and removal, the separate meetings, and the evaluation mechanism. It binds the COMPANY as well as the directors. Schedule IV is not carried item by item here.
rules.quote: The company and independent directors shall abide by the provisions specified in Schedule IV.
rules.appliesToText: Listed public company; and every other public company in the class Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 prescribes. Those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here - confirm it before relying on this row.

rules.title: An independent director is not entitled to any stock option, and may be paid only sitting fees, reimbursement and profit-related commission approved by the members
rules.detail: Granting an independent director an option is not merely irregular - s.149(9) says they are not entitled to it. The remuneration that IS permitted is fixed by the same sub-section, subject to s.197 and s.198.
rules.quote: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other provision of this Act, but subject to the provisions of sections 197 and 198, an independent director shall not be entitled to any stock option and may receive remuneration by way of fee provided under sub -section ( 5) of section 197, reimbursement of expenses for participation in the Board and other meetings and profit related commission as may be approved by the members.
rules.appliesToText: Listed public company; and every other public company in the class Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 prescribes. Those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here - confirm it before relying on this row.

rules.title: An independent director holds office for a term of up to five consecutive years, and re-appointment requires a SPECIAL resolution and disclosure in the Board report
rules.detail: An ordinary resolution does not re-appoint an independent director. The term is a maximum, not a default.
rules.quote: Subject to the provisions of section 152, an indepen dent director shall hold office for a term up to five consecutive years on the Board of a company, but shall be eligible for reappointment on passing of a special resolution by the company and disclosure of such appointment in the Board's report.
rules.appliesToText: Listed public company; and every other public company in the class Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 prescribes. Those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here - confirm it before relying on this row.

rules.title: No independent director may hold office for more than two consecutive terms, and is then ineligible for three years
rules.detail: The cooling-off is the limb most often missed, and s.149(11) adds a second condition: during those three years the person must not be appointed in or associated with the company in any other capacity, directly or indirectly.
rules.quote: Notw ithstanding anything contained in sub -section ( 10), no independent director shall hold office for more than two consecutive terms, but such independent director shall be eligible for appointment after the expiration of three years of ceasing to become an i ndependent director: Provided that an independent director shall not, during the said period of three years, be appointed in or be associated with the company in any other capacity, either directly or indirectly. Explanation.
rules.appliesToText: Listed public company; and every other public company in the class Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 prescribes. Those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here - confirm it before relying on this row.

rules.title: Independent directors are NOT liable to retire by rotation
rules.detail: s.152(6) and (7) do not apply to them. Counting an independent director into the rotating two-thirds is the error this sub-section exists to prevent, and it changes how many directors actually retire at the AGM.
rules.quote: The provisions of sub -sections ( 6) and ( 7) of section 152 in respect of retirement of directors by rotation shall not be applicable to appointment of independent directors. 150. Manner of selection of independ ent directors and maintenance of databank of independent directors.
rules.appliesToText: Listed public company; and every other public company in the class Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules 2014 prescribes. Those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here - confirm it before relying on this row.

rules.title: The Audit Committee must have a minimum of three directors with independent directors forming a MAJORITY, and a majority of members including the chairperson must be able to read and understand financial statements
rules.detail: Note the difference from LODR Reg 18(1), which requires TWO-THIRDS independent. A listed entity must meet the stricter LODR test; an unlisted company in the prescribed class meets this one.
rules.quote: The Audit Committee shall consist of a minimum of three directors with independent directors forming a majority: Provided that majority of members of Audit Committee including its Chairperson shall be persons with ability to read and understand, the financial statement.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(1) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: The Board must specify the Audit Committee terms of reference IN WRITING, covering at least the matters s.177(4) lists
rules.detail: Recommendation for appointment, remuneration and terms of the auditors; review and monitoring of their independence and audit effectiveness; examination of the financial statement and the auditors report; approval or subsequent modification of related party transactions; scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments; valuation of undertakings or assets; evaluation of internal financial controls and risk management systems; and monitoring the end use of funds raised through public offers. A committee operating without written terms does not meet s.177(4).
rules.quote: Every Audit Committee shall act in accordance with the terms of reference specified in writing by the Board which shall, inter alia, include, — (i) the recommendation for appointment , remuneration and terms of appointment of auditors of the company; (ii) review and monitor the auditor’s independence and performance, and effectiveness of audit process; (iii) examination of the financial statement and the auditors’ report thereon; (iv) approval or any subsequent modification of transactions of the company with related parties: 1.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(1) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: The Audit Committee has authority to investigate any matter in its terms of reference or referred by the Board, power to obtain outside professional advice, and FULL ACCESS to the information contained in the records of the company
rules.detail: A power the company must not obstruct, not merely one the charter may grant.
rules.quote: The Audit Committee shall have authority to investigate into any matter in relation to the items specified in sub -section ( 4) or refe rred to it by the Board and for this purpose shall have power to obtain professional advice from external sources and have full access to information contained in the records of the company.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(1) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: The auditors and the key managerial personnel have a RIGHT TO BE HEARD at Audit Committee meetings considering the auditors report, but no right to vote
rules.detail: A procedural right the company must honour when the committee considers the auditors report.
rules.quote: The auditors of a company and the key managerial personnel sh all have a right to be heard in the meetings of the Audit Committee when it considers the auditor’s report but shall not have the right to vote.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(1) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: The Board report must disclose the composition of the Audit Committee, and where the Board did not accept any recommendation of the Committee, that fact with the reasons
rules.detail: A disclosure duty sitting in s.177 rather than in s.134, which is why it is missed. The second limb bites only when the Board has declined a recommendation - and that is exactly when it matters.
rules.quote: The Board’s report under sub -section ( 3) of section 134 shall disclose the composition of an Audit Committe e and where the Board had not accepted any recommendation of the Audit Committee, the same shall be disclosed in such report along with the reasons therefor.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(1) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: Establish a vigil mechanism for directors and employees to report genuine concerns
rules.detail: Distinct from LODR Reg 22, which carries the same duty for a listed entity under the listing regulations. A company in the prescribed class owes this under the Act whether or not it is listed.
rules.quote: Every listed company or such class or classes of companies, as may be prescribed, shall establ ish a vigil mechanism for directors and employees to report genuine concerns in such manner as may be prescribed.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(9) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: The vigil mechanism must provide adequate safeguards against victimisation and DIRECT ACCESS to the chairperson of the Audit Committee in appropriate or exceptional cases
rules.detail: Both limbs. A mechanism that routes every report through management does not meet s.177(10).
rules.quote: The vigil mechanism under sub -section ( 9) shall provide for adequate safeguards against victimisation of persons who use such mechanism a nd make provision for direct access to the chairperson of the Audit Committee in appropriate or exceptional cases: Provided that the details of establishment of such mechanism shall be disclosed by the company on its website, if any, and in the Board’s rep ort. 178. Nomination and Remuneration Committee and Stakeholders Relationship Committee.
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.177(9) says "may be prescribed". Rule 6 of the Companies (Meetings of Board and its Powers) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: An individual may not be appointed auditor for more than ONE term of five consecutive years, and an audit firm for more than TWO terms of five consecutive years
rules.detail: SS2q named this as the one remaining auditor obligation worth a register and the highest-consequence one: miss it and the auditor is disqualified. It is a multi-year clock across appointments, so no date is computed from a single meeting - this app holds no auditor tenure register.
rules.quote: No listed company or a company belonging to such class or classes of companies as may be prescribed, shall appoint or re -appoint — (a) an individual as auditor for more than one term of five c onsecutive years; and (b) an audit firm as auditor for more than two terms of five consecutive years: Provided that — (i) an individual auditor who has completed his term under clause ( a) shall not be eligible for re-appointment as auditor in the same compa ny for five years from the completion of his term;
rules.appliesToText: Every listed company, and every other company in the class s.139(2) says "may be prescribed". Rule 5 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014 sets it; those Rules are NOT in reference/, so the class test cannot be evaluated here.

rules.title: The FIRST auditor must be appointed by the Board within thirty days of the date of registration; failing which the members appoint within ninety days at an extraordinary general meeting
rules.detail: Thirty days from REGISTRATION, not from the first board meeting. This app holds the incorporation year from the CIN but not the registration date, so the period is certain and the anchor is not held. The auditor so appointed holds office until the conclusion of the first annual general meeting.
rules.quote: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub -section ( 1), the first auditor of a company, other t han a Government company, shall be appointed by the Board of Directors within thirty days from the date of registration of the company and in the case of failure of the Board to appoint such auditor, it shall inform the members of the company, who shall wi thin ninety days at an extraordinary general meeting appoint such auditor and such auditor shall hold office till the conclusion of the first annual general meeting. 1. Subs.
rules.appliesToText: Every company other than a Government company

rules.title: A casual vacancy in the office of auditor is filled by the Board within thirty days; where it arose from RESIGNATION the appointment must also be approved by the members at a general meeting within three months of the Board recommendation
rules.detail: Two periods and two bodies. A resignation vacancy filled by the Board alone is not complete: the members must approve within three months. The auditor so appointed holds office to the conclusion of the next annual general meeting.
rules.quote: Any casual vacancy in the office of an auditor shall — (i) in the case of a company other than a company whose accounts a re subject to audit by an auditor appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor -General of India, be filled by the Board of Directors within thirty days, but if such casual vacancy is as a result of the resignation of an auditor, such appointment shall also be approved by the company at a general meeting convened within three months of the recommendation of the Board and he shall hold the office till the conclusion of
rules.timelineText: Within thirty days, and three months for member approval on a resignation

due.when: A casual vacancy arises in the office of auditor

rules.appliesToText: Every company other than one audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General

rules.title: Where the company must constitute an Audit Committee, every auditor appointment including a casual vacancy must be made after taking the Committee recommendation into account
rules.detail: The sequence is the obligation: the Committee recommends, then the Board or members appoint. An appointment made first and reported to the Committee afterwards does not meet s.139(11).
rules.quote: Where a company is required to constitute an Audit Committee under section 1 77, all appointments, including the filling of a casual vacancy of an auditor under this section shall be made after taking into account the recommendations of such committee. 140. Removal, resignation of auditor and giving of special notice.
